concerns.text: T100 (Phase 1) must 'import (do not duplicate) the existing code/sieve.py, code/stats.py, and code/visualize.py modules', but the tasks that produce/refine those modules (T010–T014 sieve, T015–T022b stats, T023–T029 visualize) appear LATER in Phase 2 and are UNCHECKED. This is consumer-before-producer: either the modules genuinely exist (then mark those batches checked and move them before T100) or they don't (then T100's import-based verification cannot pass). The 'Preserved as verified' label on unchecked `- [ ]` items does not resolve the ordering contradiction.

T103(a) reads 'results/reports/benchmark_N5M.json' and asserts wall time ≤ 3600 s, but no task produces benchmark_N5M.json. T102's outputs are only data/raw/residues_*.json and data/processed/stats_*.json. Missing producer task (or T102's description must be extended to emit the benchmark report) — otherwise T103 consumes a nonexistent artifact.

T101 is tagged [P] (parallel with T100), but its verification requires 'every command listed is the literal command executed by T100/T104'. T104 does not exist until Phase 2, so T101's acceptance cannot be evaluated in parallel with T100 — hidden ordering dependency. Either drop the [P] tag / move T101 after T104, or restate verification to check commands against the tasks.md text rather than executed runs.

T014 appears both in the checked foundation line ('[X] T005/T004/T007/T008/T009/T014') and inside the unchecked batch '- [ ] T010–T014'. Duplicate/contradictory completion status makes the effective execution order ambiguous; deduplicate and mark each batch's status consistently.
